OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to E.164:
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise country code
            '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits;
            spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped and the result must have 8 to 15 digits
            after the '+'. The E.164 value is stored and returned (e.g. '0412 345 678' ->
            '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            Optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' form. When
            omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to E.164:
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise country code
            '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits;
            spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped and the result must have 8 to 15 digits
            after the '+'. The E.164 value is stored and returned (e.g. '0412 345 678' ->
            '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            Optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' form. When
            omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: >-
                The pet owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName' from the
                stored first and last names.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The pet owner's initials as the upper-cased first letters of the
                stored first and last names, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3 is
                the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and NNNN is a
                global 4-digit zero-padded sequence assigned at creation.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets
    OwnerPage:
      title: Owner page
      description: A page of pet owners.
      type: object
      properties:
        content:

          description: Pet owners in the requested page.
          type: array
          items:

        page:

          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 0

          description: Requested page size.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 1
          example: 5

          title: Total elements
          description: Total number of owners matching the request.
          type: integer
          format: int64
          minimum: 0
          example: 10
        totalPages:
          title: Total pages
          description: Total number of pages matching the request.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 2

        - content

The full suite is green: **262 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors**.

## Summary

I implemented the household-uniqueness rule for creating owners. Creating an owner is now rejected with **409 Conflict** when another owner has the same last name and the same address (compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace), unless the request sets `sharesHousehold: true`.

Following the project's OfficeFloor function-injection conventions (not Spring MVC):

**New pipeline step**
- `EnsureOwnerHouseholdUnique` — reads the validated `@Val OwnerFieldsDto`, returns early when `sharesHousehold` is true, otherwise scans existing owners and throws when a normalized last-name + address match is found. Normalization = trim, collapse internal whitespace to a single space, lower-case (`Locale.ROOT`).
- Wired into `owners.POST.yml` between `ensureTelephoneUnique` and `build` (governed by the same transaction), so a clash is a 409 before any row is persisted.

**New escalation (409 handler)**
- `DuplicateHouseholdException` (checked) + `DuplicateHouseholdExceptionHandler` responding `409` with a `ProblemDetail`, plus its `officefloor/escalation/*.yml`, mirroring the existing `DuplicateTelephoneException` pattern.

**Schema**
- Added a write-only `sharesHousehold` boolean to the `OwnerFields` OpenAPI schema (generates the DTO getter; excluded from responses).

**Tests** (`OwnerRestControllerV1Tests`)
- Added `createOwnerRejectsDuplicateHousehold` (409 via case/whitespace variant of the seeded Franklin household) and `createOwnerAllowsSharedHouseholdWhenAcknowledged` (201 with `sharesHousehold:true`).
- Two pre-existing success tests (`createOwnerSuccess`, `createOwnerNormalizesTelephoneToE164`) created a Franklin at *110 W. Liberty St.* — the exact seeded household — which now legitimately conflicts under the new rule. I gave them distinct addresses so they still exercise their original intent (successful create / telephone normalization) without a spurious collision. PUT/update tests were unaffected since the rule is create-only.

One design note: the check uses `ownerRepository.findAll()` and compares in Java, because collapsing whitespace can't be expressed portably in the repository query layer, and it keeps the rule consistent across the JPA/JDBC/Spring-Data implementations.
